findings_addressed.oracle: Patch intellicrack.bridges.sandbox_bridge.importlib.import_module with a counter; clear lru_cache before the run; make TWO distinct bridge calls (extract_iocs then timeline); assert import_count == 1. The cache prevents the second bridge call from re-invoking import_module.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Remove @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=1) from _get_analysis_module in src/intellicrack/bridges/sandbox_bridge.py (line 53) — each bridge call would then call importlib.import_module independently, producing import_count==2 and failing the assert import_count == 1.

findings_addressed.oracle: Supply a fixed aware datetime in UTC-5 (timezone(timedelta(hours=-5))). Call bridge.list() via monkeypatched _manager. Parse the result strings with datetime.fromisoformat() and assert utcoffset() == timedelta(0). Also verify the round-trip value equals the original instant converted to UTC.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Remove .astimezone(UTC) from the isoformat() expression at src/intellicrack/bridges/sandbox_bridge.py line 1400 so it becomes inst.created_at.isoformat(). The output would then contain '-05:00' and datetime.fromisoformat(created_at).utcoffset() would equal timedelta(hours=-5), not timedelta(0), causing the assertion to fail.

findings_addressed.oracle: Assert result.__name__ == 'intellicrack.sandbox.analysis' and that each of the five public callables (extract_iocs, generate_timeline, match_behaviors, detect_c2_patterns, diff_reports) is callable on the returned object.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: Change importlib.import_module('intellicrack.sandbox.analysis') to importlib.import_module('intellicrack.sandbox') in src/intellicrack/bridges/sandbox_bridge.py (line 60) — __name__ would be 'intellicrack.sandbox' and the required callables would be absent, failing both assertions.

The companion test_list_normalises_non_utc_input_to_utc_offset_zero remains. FIX (2026-06-22): test_tool_def_schemas_mention_utc had a host-timezone-dependent 'naive' input case whose oracle wrongly assumed production does value.replace(tzinfo=UTC); production actually does .astimezone(UTC), which interprets naive datetimes as host-local time. In a non-UTC container naive 12:00 became 18:00 UTC, failing the round-trip. Replaced the naive case with a second aware non-UTC offset (UTC-5) so all three inputs (UTC, UTC-5, UTC+9) are deterministic and falsifiable. Verified GREEN in sandbox.
